stem:
Nalini draws the irregular closed shape shown in the diagram on 1 cm² squared paper.

How should she estimate its area in square centimetres?

options.text: Count every whole square fully inside the shape and estimate each partly covered square as a fraction of one square centimetre.
Answer with the words squared paper; that label is the estimate.
The squared paper produces the shape, so the area equals the area of the whole grid.
Measure the perimeter of the shape in centimetres and take that number as the area.

teacher.key_rationale: On 1 cm² paper, area is estimated by counting full interior squares and estimating partial squares. Naming squared paper is not a method. The grid does not produce the shape. Perimeter is a different quantity.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote kite to an irregular closed polygon on an 8 by 6 one-centimetre grid.
